name: Family/dependent sponsorship (spouse and children)

requirements.blocker_text: The sponsor must hold a valid Iqama (or Premium Residency) with at least 3-6 months of remaining validity at the time of application.
requirements.fix_path: Ensure the sponsor's Iqama has sufficient remaining validity before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: The sponsor's profession, as classified on their Iqama, must be on the Ministry of Interior's approved list for family sponsorship -- most labourer/basic-tier occupations do not qualify.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the Iqama profession classification qualifies, or have the employer update it to an eligible category where accurate.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a documented salary of roughly SAR 4,000-10,000/month depending on the profession category and number of dependents being sponsored, confirmed via the sponsor's GOSI (social insurance) certificate.
requirements.fix_path: Document a salary meeting the applicable threshold for the number and type of dependents being sponsored.

evidence_required.document: Attested marriage/birth certificates for each dependent
Registered tenancy contract (Ejar) in the sponsor's name

outcome.duration_length: tied to the sponsor's Iqama validity

sources.title: KSA Expats -- Permanent Family Visa Saudi Arabia 2026 guide
Incorp MENA -- Saudi Dependent & Family Visa: Eligibility & Process 2026

notes: STATUS: DRAFT, and an unusually explicit sourcing gap for this dataset. The family-sponsorship salary threshold in Saudi Arabia is genuinely NOT a single published statutory figure -- one of the sources checked in this research pass states this outright ('Saudi Arabia's dependent visa salary threshold is not published as a fixed figure'), and the range cited across independent secondary sources spans SAR 3,500 to SAR 10,000/month depending on profession, number of dependents, and which Jawazat office processes the application. No primary MOI, Jawazat, or Absher page with a clean, citable, single figure was found in this research pass despite multiple targeted searches -- this is a genuine, honestly-reported sourcing gap rather than a resolved fact, consistent with this project's discipline of flagging what it doesn't know rather than inventing a precise number. resolved SAR 4,000 is used as the requirement's floor because it is the most consistently-cited baseline figure and matches the SAR 4,000 Nitaqat/Saudization compliance threshold that several sources appear to be extrapolating the family-visa figure from -- but this extrapolation is itself unconfirmed against a primary source, and the true rule may be entirely discretionary/administrative rather than a fixed number at all. A follow-up session should attempt direct outreach to moi.gov.sa or absher.sa (both currently inaccessible to automated fetching) to resolve this properly before promoting this route to published status. Note on family_can_join: set to false here because this route's own holder is the dependent (spouse/child) being sponsored -- a dependent Iqama does not itself carry the right to further sponsor sub-dependents; that would require the dependent to first obtain independent, primary-holder status.
